Lemma
[Upper bound for the Laplacian of distance] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0064, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0065, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0066 ↗ def:chow-iii-laplacian-upper-barrier 1. ch18:18.6\group Distance Barriers

Let $(\mathcal M^n,g)$ be complete, let $x\ne x_0$, and let $\gamma :[0,s_0]\to \mathcal M$ be a unit-speed minimizing geodesic from $x_0$ to $x$. For every continuous piecewise smooth $\zeta :[0,s_0]\to [0,1]$ with $\zeta (0)=0$ and $\zeta (s_0)=1$, \[ \Delta _gd_g(x_0,x)\le \int _0^{s_0} \bigl((n-1)(\zeta ')^2-\zeta ^2\Ric (\gamma ',\gamma ')\bigr)\, \dd s \] in the barrier sense.
Proof

\sketch Vary $\gamma $ through paths whose endpoint moves by the exponential map at $x$, using variation fields $\zeta E_i$, where the $E_i$ are parallel orthonormal fields normal to $\gamma '$. Their lengths define a smooth upper barrier for distance. Summing the second variation formula over the $n-1$ normal directions gives

\[ \sum _{i=1}^{n-1}\int _0^{s_0} \bigl((\zeta ')^2-\zeta ^2\langle R(\gamma ',E_i)E_i,\gamma '\rangle \bigr)\, \dd s, \]

which is the displayed expression after taking the trace of curvature.

□
